items.title: AAP alleges fraud as Raghav Chadha makes it to Delhi voter rolls
items.summary: Deleted in Punjab’s special intensive revision, Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha’s name is now available in Delhi’s draft roll. The BJP leader’s name is at serial number 747 in part 46 of the Rajinder Nagar assembly, as per Election Commission’s website. The draft roll for part 46 that was published on August 31 had ended with 746 voters. The final roll is set to be published only in November after the objections round. Chadha was earlier registered as a voter in Punjab’s SAS Nagar constituency, better known as Mohali, and had voted from there during the 2024 Lok Sabha election. He was not part of the draft roll published in Punjab earlier in August and was marked “permanently shifted”. He had called it “vendetta”. The final roll is scheduled to be published on October 12. This comes days after the Aam Aadmi Party and certain media reports hinted that the BJP leader was trying to get a “backdoor” entry into the voter rolls. The party repeated these allegations on Tuesday, accusing the Election Commission of “farziwada”. items.title: Bharat Ratna CNR Rao gets named in SIR notice list, ECI then backtracks
items.summary: Eminent scientist and Bharat Ratna awardee CNR Rao’s name has appeared on the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer’s list of electors flagged for notices during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) over a discrepancy in his electoral records. Election authorities, however, say no notice was served on the 92-year-old scientist, raising questions over how his name came to figure on the list. According to ECI, Professor Rao is a voter in Part No 59 of the Malleswaram Assembly constituency. Under the SIR process, notices are generated for electors whose records are flagged for discrepancies or cannot be mapped to the 2002 electoral roll. The SIR notice phase covers electors whose records fall under the “no mapping” or “anomalies” categories. More than 43.81 lakh notices have been generated across Karnataka, of which 7.31 lakh had been delivered as of September 4. The notices are handed over to Booth Level Officers (BLOs), who are responsible for delivering them to voters, while the subsequent verification is conducted by the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) or Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO). items.title: COVID-19 protests: Supreme Court allows Himachal Pradesh to withdraw cases against MLAs/MPs
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday permitted Himachal Pradesh government to withdraw prosecutions in 45 criminal cases registered by the State police against sitting and former lawmakers during the COVID-19 pandemic in connection with protests and voicing of public grievances. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana set aside Himachal Pradesh High Court's decision to permit withdrawal of only 20 of the 65 cases involving Members of Parliament (MPs) and Members of Legislative Assembly (MLAs). The High Court’s approval was required in view of the apex court’s 2021 judgment in the Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay case, which mandates strict judicial scrutiny to curb the misuse of executive power in dropping prosecutions against lawmakers. Today, the top court said that none of the cases involving the lawmakers in Himachal Pradesh disclosed the commission of grave or heinous crimes. It also noted that in the four of the 45 cases not permitted to be withdrawn by the High Court, the trials resulted in acquittal or "dismissal". items.title: Good ideas no longer need a sponsor before they can exist: vibecode.law co-founder Alex Baker
items.summary: The Indian LegalTech Network (ILTN) and vibecode.law have launched the Vibeathon 2026, billed as India’s first “vibe-coding” hackathon for lawyers. The initiative gives lawyers, law students and other legal professionals three weeks to identify problems in legal practice and build working solutions using AI-assisted coding platforms. Participants do not need prior coding experience, with the organisers seeking to demonstrate how AI can lower the barriers to building software for legal practice. vibecode.law, launched earlier this year by Chris Bridges of Tacit Legal, Matt Pollins of Lupl and Alex Baker of Legal Tech Collective, began as a weekend project between its three founders. Baker noted that the platform has since seen hundreds of lawyers from around the world build a wide variety of applications and share them with others exploring legal technology. Baker further spoke about what prompted the creation of vibecode.law, where lawyers should begin if they have never coded before, the limits of AI-built prototypes and what vibe coding could mean for innovation within law firms. items.title: Supreme Court flags irrelevant evidence in corruption cases; acquits public servant in 1993 case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday criticised the use of voluminous and irrelevant evidence in corruption cases while acquitting a former public servant in a case dating back to 1993 [ Khanindra Kr Dutta v. CBI ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran noted that the prosecution had examined 62 witnesses, while the High Court had referred to the evidence of only 9 of them. The Court said that lengthy evidence in corruption cases could often intimidate courts, particularly when much of the material was not relevant. “In corruption cases voluminous evidence is led, which is often intimidating to the Court, especially since many aspects attempted to be led in evidence are way off the mark, in providing a substantiation of the allegation, or to bring home the guilt of the accused-public servant...Prosecution in corruption cases have a history of long pendency; especially because of the voluminous evidence led, which often is unnecessary and as we noticed, mostly irrelevant," it said. items.title: Offerings made to hereditary temple priest are his personal income, not joint family wealth: Karnataka HC
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that offerings made to hereditary temple priests form part of their personal income and not joint family wealth, meaning that property bought using such income would also be personal assets and not joint family property [ Rajamati v Leelavathi ]. A Bench Justices R Nataraj and Tyagaraja N Inavally made the observation while dealing with a family dispute over property purchased using the earnings of a deceased Hindu priest. "If such person, in deference to the traditions in the family, endows himself in the service of the deity and devotees show obeisance to him by offering cash or in kind, then such offerings would be in recognition of the man's service and hence, should be construed as his individual income," the Court said. The Court, however, also clarified that not all offerings made by devotees at a temple accrue to the priest personally. It held that where a trust has been constituted to administer the temple, offerings made by devotees to the temple go into the trust's accounts and cannot be treated as the priest's personal income. items.title: Why courts extend arbitration deadlines, not replace arbitrators? Justice Bharati Dangre explains
items.summary: Replacing an arbitrator after years of hearings can wipe out substantial time, money and effort already spent in the proceedings, Bombay High Court judge Justice Bharati Dangre said while explaining why courts often grant extensions under Section 29A of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act. " If I turn it down today and appoint a new arbitrator, what happens to all that effort, all that resources which have gone for all these years? " Justice Dangre said. She added that courts may therefore grant a short extension if it ultimately serves the interests of justice. Justice Dangre was speaking during a fireside chat with Senior Advocate Vikram Nankani at India ADR Week 2026 in Mumbai, organised by the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA). During the discussion, Nankani asked about her transition from Nagpur to Mumbai and her experience of handling commercial matters. Justice Dangre said that her earlier practice, largely involving civil and criminal matters for the government, had given her little exposure to arbitration. items.title: The $1 trillion digital ambition hits its regulatory clock: Managing enterprise risk under India's DPDP regime
items.summary: As India targets a $1 trillion digital economy by 2030, the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, along with the DPDP Rules, 2025, introduces a fundamental shift in legal liability for corporate India. The regulatory landscape transitions from simple policy compliance to strict statutory fiduciary accountability. With the principal operational rules taking full effect on 13 May 2027, boardrooms face immediate legal and operational obligations. Navigating the phased commencement clock Managing compliance requires aligning corporate workflows with statutory deadlines: Nov 13, 2025 | Initial administrative and framework rules commenced. Nov 13, 2026 | Rule 4 (Consent Manager Framework) goes live. May 13, 2027 | Become fully enforceable. Treating May 13, 2027 as a deferred deadline exposes companies to significant regulatory risk. Conducting enterprise-wide data mapping, amending vendor contracts, restructuring notice procedures, and building defensible audit trails requires extended lead time. items.title: NLIU team wins MMCS International Maritime Arbitration Competition 2026 in Maldives
items.summary: A team of four students from the National Law Institute University (NLIU), Bhopal has won the Maldives Moot Court Society (MMCS) International Maritime Arbitration Competition (MIMAC) 2026. The team comprised Manan Budhiraja , Soumil Srivastava , Rohini Garg and Tanishka Sinha . The competition was held in the Maldives and drew teams from several countries. MIMAC is organised by the Maldives Moot Court Society. Teams are required to draft written submissions as both Claimant and Respondent, followed by oral arguments before a panel of arbitrators and academics. The winning team receives a cash prize of $1,000, along with internships and certificates. The NLIU Bhopal team acknowledged the contribution of Rahul Mishra, who provided guidance and support throughout their preparation.

items.title: Marriage doesn't mean extinction of individual autonomy but can marital rape be prosecuted? Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court will commence hearing the batch of petitions seeking criminalisation of marital rape from next month. Currently, marital rape is excluded from the ambit of the offence of "rape" by way of Exception 2 to Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). A similar provision is also present in the newly enacted Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the IPC in 2023. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana on Wednesday directed that the matter be listed for final hearing after three weeks on Wednesdays and Thursdays. The Court passed the direction after noting that the Central government has filed its affidavit in the matter. "The Union Government has filed its reply in the connected matters also. A copy thereof shall be supplied to all learned counsel appearing in the connected cases within two days. We are informed that the other pleadings are complete. items.title: CCI dismisses Kerala private bus operators’ plea against free KSRTC bus travel for women
items.summary: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has dismissed a challenge by private bus operators to Kerala’s Priyadarshini Scheme, which provides free travel to women and transgender persons in buses operated by the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC). The Commission held that a State-funded welfare scheme would not ordinarily attract competition law scrutiny merely because it causes a commercial disadvantage to private operators. A Bench comprising CCI Chairperson Ravneet Kaur and Members Sweta Kakkad and Deepak Anurag passed the order on September 8. “ The formulation and implementation of a welfare scheme by the Government, aimed at public welfare, would not ordinarily invite scrutiny under the Act, ” the CCI said. The Commission added that any differential commercial impact on private operators resulting from such a policy measure could not, by itself, be treated as a contravention of the Competition Act. The complaint was filed by two private stage carriage operators in Kerala alleging abuse of dominant position under Section 4 of the Competition Act by the State government and KSRTC. items.title: Sharia body can't decide whether Muslim woman is divorced: Chhattisgarh High Court
items.summary: A private Sharia body has no legal authority to decide whether a Muslim woman is legally divorced or to determine her marital status, the Chhattisgarh High Court recently held. In a judgment delivered on September 7, Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad said that such adjudicatory power must flow from a law enacted by a competent legislature and cannot be assumed by a private religious institution. The Court was dealing with a challenge to a January 2022 communication issued by the Idara-E-Shariya Islami Court at Raipur which declared that the petitioner, a Muslim woman, had been divorced by her husband. " Religion may guide an individual's conscience and personal faith, but no religious institution or private body can be permitted to assume the authority of a Court established by law or to use religious belief as a means of determining or enforcing the legal status and rights of an individual. The rule of law and the constitutional framework remain paramount, " the Court said. items.title: TN Smart City Mission: 52 projects not implemented, 44 unplanned ones taken up, finds CAG
items.summary: A Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) report on the implementation of the Smart City Mission (SCM) in Tamil Nadu found that 52 approved projects, valued at Rs 1,602.20 crore were not implemented. It also found that 44 projects valued at Rs 623.86 crore that were not originally planned were implemented. This was in violation of project guidelines, the report noted. The 52 approved projects were included in the plan after consultation with the public. The performance audit conducted by the CAG noted that Tamil Nadu faces several shortcomings in the implementation of SCM, including diversion of funds, unplanned projects, delays and lack of operational independence of the Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs). The SCM was launched by the Union government in 2015 to develop 100 cities. In Tamil Nadu, 11 cities were selected. The audit examined seven of the 11 cities in the state, namely, Chennai, Coimbatore, Erode, Salem, Madurai, Tirunelveli, and Tiruppur. items.title: Arrogance: Supreme Court initiates contempt case against Yatharth Hospital for ignoring court notice in EWS case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday initiated formal contempt of court proceedings against Yatharth Hospital for filing an “ex facie false” affidavit claiming that it had not received a notice issued by the Court. Moolchand Khairati Ram Trust] A Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar passed the order in proceedings concerning the obligation of private hospitals allotted government land at concessional rates to provide free treatment to patients from economically weaker sections (EWS). Yatharth Hospital claimed that it learnt about the court proceedings only through informal communication and industry peers, and not through formal service of notice by the Court. However, the Bench found that this assertion was contradicted by the Court’s office report dated April 22, which clearly recorded that the notice had been served.
